**About Flatpay

**Flatpay makes card payments simple and fair for small businesses. Marketing is central to how we grow, and we run it as a measurable acquisition engine where curiosity, experimentation and commercial results drive our decisions.

We are looking for an Affiliate & Partnerships Manager to lead our network of affiliates, publishers and lead generation partners across all of our markets.

The role

In six months, affiliate went from zero to one of our most important channels. Now we need someone to take it further.

You like meeting people, spotting opportunities and turning a good conversation into a partnership that performs. You can negotiate a strong deal and still leave the other side wanting to work with you again. And signing is only the start: you will follow each partnership through the funnel, understand what makes it profitable and make it better.

This is a group function. You will report to our Head of Group Marketing, work with colleagues across creative, paid media and analytics, and have real autonomy. We want fewer approval steps, not more. You will need to be self-driven, and in return you will learn a lot across teams and functions.

**What You'll Do

**

• Find new partners. Identify promising affiliates, publishers and lead generation partners, start the conversations and build a pipeline across our markets.

• Negotiate deals that last. Agree pricing, commission structures and terms that support profitable growth for us and a sustainable relationship for them.

• Turn good partners into great ones. Set clear expectations and help partners improve their campaigns, placements and results.

• Look beyond the lead. Follow the journey from lead to booked meeting to customer, and weigh acquisition cost against customer value.

• Make the call. Recommend when to scale, renegotiate, pause or end a partnership.

• Fix what is leaking. Work with partners, the analytics team and sales to find where performance breaks down, then test hypotheses.

• Own the roadmap and reporting. Set the partner roadmap, run onboarding, tracking and commission validation, and report on what the channel delivers.

• Work smarter with AI. Use AI as an assistant to find partners, analyse results and speed up daily work. It supports your judgement and never replaces it.

**How We Work

**

• Quality first, then scale. We would rather have fewer, better leads than many weak ones, but we are not afraid to test. One high-potential partner was trialled in one market and, two months later, was live in five and our biggest partner in the group.

• Shared decisions where it counts. You will set commission models and budgets together with the Head of Group Marketing, so we stay aligned across channels.

**Who You Are

**

• You have experience in affiliate marketing, performance partnerships or lead generation, with responsibility for partner relationships and measurable results.

• You are a strong negotiator who understands the other side’s incentives and can have a direct conversation when something needs to change.

• You are commercially sharp and comfortable turning data and spreadsheets into a clear recommendation.

• You are curious. You ask why, test your assumptions and change your mind when the evidence says so.

• You take initiative and follow through, and you are happy moving fast where not every process exists yet.

• You communicate clearly in English. Additional languages are a plus.

Experience with B2B lead generation, platforms such as Impact, Awin or PartnerStack, or tracking and attribution is an advantage. We can more about your judgement, results and ability to learn than about tool familiarity.

What we offer

• Real ownership of the partner roadmap and a direct hand in growing a channel that grows with the company

• Competitive salary based on your qualifications

• A central marketing team and a manager who will support your development

• Room to build processes, try new approaches and shape the future of affiliate at Flatpay

**Why Flatpay

**Joining Flatpay means stepping into a dynamic environment where innovation is encouraged, and teamwork is celebrated. Here, you'll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact, contributing to our mission of empowering merchants to succeed.

With us, you’ll experience an ambitious drive to constantly push boundaries and redefine what's possible. While we don’t take ourselves too seriously, we take our responsibility towards our people very seriously. We welcome driven, low-ego individuals who live our values and want to grow with us.

Established in 2022 in Copenhagen with a commitment to transparency, we've streamlined card payments to small and medium-sized businesses. Our innovative pricing model eliminates hidden costs and fees, offering a simple flat rate for all cards with no monthly subscription for our point-of-sale and payment solutions.

Operating in Denmark, Finland, Germany, Italy, France, the United Kingdom, and the Netherlands, we're more than just a service provider; we are your trusted business partner.

We continuously strive to stay ahead of the curve, adapting our solutions to meet our clients' evolving needs. Ready to be part of something extraordinary?

Senior Utility Engineer – Plant Engineering (Søborg)

Keep life-changing therapies moving by keeping our utilities running.

Location: Søborg, Denmark. Please note that AGC Biologics does not offer relocation assistance. Applicants must already reside in Denmark or the Greater Malmö area in Sweden.

AGC Biologics is expanding its Utility team in Søborg and is looking for an experienced Senior Utility Engineer with strong expertise in GMP-regulated pharmaceutical water systems. You will play an important role in ensuring the safe, reliable and compliant operation of utility systems that support our 24/7 research, development and production activities.

About the department

The Utility team is responsible for critical utility systems that support production and laboratory operations at our Søborg site. These include pharmaceutical water systems and other essential utilities. You will work closely with Production, QA, Validation, Maintenance and Project teams in a regulated environment where reliability, compliance and patient safety are key priorities.

The role

As Senior Utility Engineer, you will take technical ownership of GMP-critical water systems across the site. This is a hands-on, operational role focused on compliance, troubleshooting, risk reduction and continuous improvement. You will work alongside two skilled technicians who carry out scheduled and unscheduled maintenance, while you focus on system performance, technical oversight and long-term improvements.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Ensuring the stable, compliant and efficient operation of pharmaceutical water systems.

• Taking technical ownership of systems and driving improvements to reliability and performance.

• Maintaining technical documentation, including SOPs, P&IDs and maintenance plans, in line with GMP requirements.

• Leading troubleshooting, root cause analysis, risk assessments and CAPA activities.

• Supporting commissioning, qualification and handover of utility projects to Operations and Maintenance.

• Providing technical input to CAPEX and OPEX projects.

• Representing Utilities during audits and inspections.

• Acting as the senior technical contact for water systems and providing guidance to colleagues across the site.

Most work takes place during regular business hours, although occasional evening or weekend work may be required to support our 24/7 production environment.

Initially, your primary focus will be pharmaceutical water systems. Over time, your responsibilities may expand to include black and clean utilities, allowing you to contribute more broadly across the Utility team.

Experience and competences

We are looking for an experienced Senior Utility Engineer with substantial experience working with pharmaceutical water systems in a GMP-regulated environment.

To succeed in the role, you have:

• An engineering degree in mechanical, electrical or chemical engineering, or a similar field, or an equivalent technical background combined with relevant experience.

• Strong knowledge of pharmaceutical water systems and applicable GMP/GxP requirements.

• Experience with troubleshooting, maintenance and optimisation of technical systems.

• Experience with technical documentation, deviations, CAPAs, risk assessments and regulatory inspections.

• The ability to take technical ownership, solve complex problems and drive improvements independently.

• The ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams and communicate technical information clearly.

Experience with GMP utilities, project handovers, black and clean utilities, regulatory audits and mentoring colleagues is an advantage.

As a person, you are

You are proactive, independent and comfortable taking ownership of your responsibilities. You are structured and solution-oriented, with a strong focus on quality and compliance. You communicate clearly, collaborate effectively across teams and enjoy sharing knowledge with colleagues. You are comfortable balancing operational priorities with technical documentation and continuous improvement.

AGC offers

At AGC Biologics, you will work with critical utility systems in a dynamic pharmaceutical production environment. You will join a collaborative team where knowledge sharing, ownership and practical problem-solving are valued. The role offers the opportunity to develop your technical expertise and contribute to the reliable operation of systems that support our production activities around the clock.

How to apply

Please submit your application and CV through the AGC Biologics career site. We do not accept applications by email.

Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, and we reserve the right to close the vacancy before the deadline if a suitable candidate is found.

Please note that AGC Biologics does not offer relocation assistance. Applicants must already reside in Denmark or the Greater Malmö area in Sweden.

We look forward to receiving your application!

Who We Are

AGC Biologics is a global Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization with a strong presence in Denmark. From our Søborg site, we develop and manufacture life‑changing advanced biologics for some of the world’s most innovative pharmaceutical companies. Together with our team members across Europe, the U.S., and Japan, we deliver development and manufacturing of mammalian and microbial-based therapeutic proteins, plasmid DNA (pDNA), messenger RNA (mRNA), viral vectors, and genetically engineered cells therapies. Across our global network, we are united by one mission: To work side by side with our customers in order to improve patients’ lives by bringing new biopharmaceuticals to market.

jobs.description:
A clinical position as staff specialist of Paediatrics at the Department of Paediatrics and Adolescent Medicine at Zealand University Hospital is open for appointment from as soon as possible.

The position as staff specialist is combined with a 5-year externally funded position as clinical associate professor (research) in Paediatrics at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen.

With this new position the Department of Paediatrics and Adolescent Medicine, Zealand University Hospital wishes to strengthen the leadership in clinical research and teaching in collaboration with the University of Copenhagen.

It is a requirement that the applicant is accepted for appointment of both the clinical associate professorship (research) and the clinical position.

About the Department

The Department of Paediatrics and Adolescent Medicine at Zealand University Hospital is a well-established clinical and research-active department with sites in Roskilde (planned move to Køge 2028) and Nykøbing Falster. The department provides comprehensive care across the full spectrum of paediatrics, including specialised services within paediatric endocrinology and the management of childhood diabetes.

The treatment of childhood diabetes in Region Zealand is organised across multiple sites, enabling strong cross-site collaboration and the development of shared clinical pathways. The department works closely with Steno Diabetes Center Zealand and collaborates with paediatric departments both within and beyond the region.

The department offers a dynamic research environment with a focus on strengthening clinical research, including dedicated research within childhood diabetes. This field involves distinct clinical and developmental considerations compared to adult diabetes, and research activities address treatment outcomes, patient development, quality of life and health equality.

Teaching and supervision of medical students and junior doctors are integral parts of the department’s activities, and there is a strong emphasis on developing future clinicians and clinical researchers.

Qualifications:

Applicants for a position as staff specialist must be board-certified specialist in Paediatrics.

Conditions:

In order to be considered, the applicant must send an application to both the Faculty (the clinical associate professorship (research)) and to the hospital (the clinical position) cf. the simultaneously advertised position of the clinical associate professorship (research). Appointment is conditioned by the fact that the applicant obtains both positions. This also applies to the applicants who are already employed as staff specialists at Zealand University Hospital.

Salary and conditions of employment as staff specialist are as agreed between the Danish Regions and the Danish Association of Medical Specialists and between the Capital Region/Region Zealand and University of Copenhagen.

As clinical associate professor (research) at least 50 % of the working time will be allocated to academic tasks (e.g. research, teaching, evaluation tasks and communication with the public) in agreement with the Head of Department of Clinical Medicine at the University of Copenhagen. The remaining time will be allocated for clinical work in agreement with the head of Department of Paediatrics and Adolescent Medicine.

Application procedure:

The application must include the following:

• Curriculum Vitae and a complete list of publications

• A description of how the applicant is qualified as

- Clinical expert

- Communicator

- Collaborator

- Manager/administrator/organizer

- Health advocate

- Scholar/researcher/teacher, professional

For more information please refer to https://sundhedsstyrelsen.dk/en/news/2013/the-seven-roles-of-physicians.

For applicants with a foreign license also a copy of the authorization certificate for specialist in Paediatrics recognition.

The closing date for applications is 30.11.2026.

Further information:

For further information please contact Head of Department of Paediatrics and Adolescent Medicine, Malene Boas, mboa@regionsjaelland.dk

The advertisement for the clinical associate professorship (research) is available from the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen

jobs.description:
**Shape the engineering solutions behind vaccines that protect lives every day

**Are you an experienced bioprocess engineer who combines deep technical expertise with the ability to set direction and bring people together?

Join Bavarian Nordic and take a leading role in shaping the processes and systems that support our Drug Substance manufacturing.

From major capital projects and technology transfers to solving complex manufacturing challenges, you will help ensure our processes are robust, scalable, and ready for reliable operation.

**Your impact

**As Senior Engineering Specialist, you will serve as a technical authority for integrated bioprocess systems across process engineering, automation, filtration, and equipment design.

You will guide critical technical decisions throughout the manufacturing lifecycle—from concept and scale-up through qualification, validation, and continuous improvement.

This is a senior individual-contributor role with broad technical responsibility and influence across functions and projects. You will lead technical workstreams and mentor experienced engineers without formal line-management responsibility.

**What You Will Do

**Working closely with Manufacturing, Engineering, Automation, Quality, Validation, and external partners, you will:

• Lead bioprocess design and optimization: Set the technical direction for upstream and downstream processes, purification, bulk formulation, and sterile transfers. Use process knowledge, modelling, and manufacturing data to improve yield, capacity, reliability, and product quality.

• Shape automation and control strategies: Translate process needs into requirements for PLC/DCS and SCADA systems, recipes, sequences, interlocks, and alarms. Ensure solutions support effective process control, data integrity, and reliable operation.

• Provide technical leadership for filtration: Define filter selection, sizing, validation, and integrity-testing strategies for liquid and gas systems. Lead investigations into filter failures, pressure deviations, and performance issues.

• Guide equipment and system design: Review and approve tanks, piping, pumps, valves, and instrumentation, including hydraulic calculations, pressure distribution, and pressure-testing strategies. Lead technical decisions for Cleaning-in-Place and Sterilization-in-Place (CIP/SIP) systems.

• Deliver projects and technology transfers: Lead process engineering activities from concept and vendor selection through factory and site acceptance testing, commissioning, qualification, process validation, and handover to operations.

• Strengthen technical standards and compliance: Resolve complex investigations, support change controls and CAPAs, and represent engineering during audits and inspections. Establish reusable design standards and share knowledge across projects and teams.

**What You Bring

**You have a master’s degree or PhD in Bioengineering, Biochemical or Chemical Engineering, Biotechnology, Mechanical Engineering, or a closely related discipline.

You bring substantial industrial experience, typically 15 years or more, including at least 10 years within pharmaceutical, biotechnology or vaccine manufacturing.

Your experience includes:

• Leading complex engineering projects as a lead engineer or technical authority, with hands-on expertise in bioprocess development, scale-up, commercial manufacturing, and lifecycle management.

• Integrating process equipment with automation and SCADA systems, including control strategies, computerized-system validation, and data integrity.

• Designing and validating filtration systems, including filter integrity testing and pressure/flow troubleshooting.

• Working with hygienic tanks and piping, hydraulic calculations, pressure testing, CIP/SIP, and contamination control.

• Leading commissioning, qualification, process validation, Process Performance Qualification, and technology transfer, supported by a strong understanding of GMP and quality risk management.

• Setting technical standards, mentoring experienced engineers, and influencing decisions across functions without relying on formal authority.

**How You Work

**You combine scientific depth with practical engineering judgement. You can move from detailed technical analysis to clear recommendations that help colleagues and leaders make informed decisions.

You take ownership, challenge assumptions constructively, and remain focused when problems span multiple systems or disciplines. Whether working with operators, specialists, suppliers, or senior stakeholders, you communicate clearly and build trust through sound decisions and consistent follow-through.

You also enjoy developing others. Sharing expertise, coaching colleagues, and creating common standards are natural parts of how you work.

**Why join Bavarian Nordic?

**At Bavarian Nordic, we work to protect lives through vaccines. In this role, you will help build and improve the manufacturing capabilities that make that purpose possible.

You will have the opportunity to influence major technical decisions, strengthen engineering practices, and see your work translate into measurable improvements in manufacturing performance and reliable supply.

Our values—Persisting Pioneers, Embracing Change, and Boosted by the Team—shape how we collaborate and solve challenges. For the right candidate, sustained performance may open opportunities for broader engineering leadership or formal people management.

**Ready to shape the future of our Drug Substance manufacturing?

**We look forward to receiving your application and learning how your technical expertise and leadership could strengthen Bavarian Nordic.

We kindly request that headhunters or recruitment agencies refrain from contacting us regarding this position.

_Bavarian Nordic is a global vaccine company with a mission to improve health and save lives through innovative vaccines. We are a preferred supplier of mpox and smallpox vaccines to governments to enhance public health preparedness and have a leading portfolio of travel vaccines. We are headquartered in Denmark and have manufacturing, research, and sales offices across Europe and North America.

_Bavarian Nordic is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applications will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against based on race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status.

For more information, visit _www.bavarian-nordic.com

With an impressive pipeline and many ongoing clinical trials, you will have a central role in supporting inspection readiness across our late-stage clinical development portfolio. Your work will help ensure that documentation is complete, compliant and readily available to support the successful execution of business-critical GMP and GCP inspections.

You will support inspection readiness activities within Global Clinical Supply, collecting, organizing and performing completeness and compliance checks of trial-specific documentation. Working closely with Clinical Supply Managers in the Portfolio & Project Delivery team and colleagues across the department, you will support selected operational tasks and initiatives while gaining broader exposure to clinical trial management. The position is based in Copenhagen.

**Responsibilities

**

• Support inspection readiness across late-stage clinical trials by collecting, organizing and maintaining relevant clinical supply documentation.

• Perform completeness and compliance checks of trial-specific documentation against applicable procedures and inspection-readiness expectations.

• Participate in back-office activities during GMP and GCP inspections, including document retrieval, request coordination and tracking of responses and follow-up items.

• Support preparation for mock inspections, audits and health authority inspections, including compilation and review of supporting documentation for completeness and readiness.

• Support activities related to day-to-day trial management, including coordination, follow-up and preparation of relevant material and documentation.

• Support distribution and logistics, including tasks related to shipment documentation, in alignment with the Drug Supply Managers.

• Build knowledge of especially GCP but also GMP and clinical supply activities within Global Clinical Supply, Portfolio & Project Delivery function

**

• Minimum a bachelor’s degree or equivalent.

• Some experience working with documentation, quality or compliance activities in the pharmaceutical, biotech, clinical research or another regulated environment is an advantage.

• Knowledge and understanding of GCP and GMP; experience with inspection or audit readiness is an advantage.

• Strong interest in documentation, quality and compliance, with a structured and detail-oriented approach to your work.

• Ability to coordinate activities, maintain structure and follow up on actions involving multiple stakeholders.

• Ability to work successfully under pressure in a fast-paced environment and with tight timelines, including during inspections.

• Ability to be proactive, enthusiastic, curious and goal orientated, with a willingness to learn new GCP/GMP-related activities.

• A team player with demonstrated ability to work effectively cross-functional with internal and external stakeholders.

• Strong communication skills in English - both oral and written.

**You will be part of a highly competent team focused on end-to-end trial management including planning and maintenance of supplies for clinical trials, working closely with cross-functional stakeholders in both CMC and Clinical Trial Operations.

DKK544.000,00---816.000,00

About Teton

Teton is building the autonomous operating system for care. Our technology gives senior living and care teams greater visibility into resident wellbeing, movement, sleep, and care delivery, helping them respond faster, work more efficiently, and provide more personalized care.

The Role

The Finance Systems Engineer will own the systems, data infrastructure, and internal tooling that power Teton’s finance function.

As Teton continues to scale, we need reliable financial data, connected systems, and automated workflows that allow the business to operate efficiently and make informed decisions. You will help strengthen our operational finance capabilities by ensuring our data is accurate, our systems work as intended, and our internal processes are scalable.

This is a hands-on role at the intersection of finance, systems engineering, and data. You will build integrations between our accounting platform, ERP, CRM, and internal product systems, develop tools that make business intelligence data easier to access, and establish controls that maintain data integrity.

What You’ll Own

Finance Data and Systems Infrastructure

• 
Own the systems and data flows supporting Teton’s finance function, ensuring financial information is accurate, accessible, and reliable.

• 
Maintain and improve integrations between accounting, ERP, CRM, and internal product systems.

• 
Identify infrastructure gaps and implement scalable solutions that support Teton’s growth.

Systems Integrations and Automation

• 
Build and maintain integrations and automated workflows that reduce manual work across finance and business operations.

• 
Troubleshoot integration issues, resolve data discrepancies, and implement lasting technical solutions.

• 
Identify opportunities to streamline processes through automation and better system design.

Data Integrity and Financial Controls

• 
Develop internal tools and automated checks to identify missing data, inconsistencies, and potential errors across systems.

• 
Establish reliable reconciliation processes and improve the traceability of financial data.

• 
Strengthen data validation and controls to support accurate reporting and dependable financial operations.

Operational Finance Support

• 
Partner with the finance team to improve day-to-day workflows, reporting capabilities, and access to business-critical information.

• 
Translate operational needs into practical technical solutions that reduce administrative overhead.

• 
Build a scalable systems foundation that supports increasingly sophisticated financial and business intelligence needs.

What Success Looks Like

In your first year, you will have:

• 
Built a reliable, scalable finance systems infrastructure with accurate data and strong integrations across accounting, ERP, CRM, and internal platforms.

• 
Automated key workflows and implemented data validation tools that reduce manual work, improve data integrity, and strengthen financial controls.

• 
Improved access to business intelligence and streamlined finance operations to support Teton’s continued growth.

What We’re Looking For

• 
Experience in finance systems, data engineering, business systems, or a similar technical role.

• 
Degree in Finance, Engineering, Analytics, or a related field.

• 
Strong technical skills in integrations, automation, APIs, and data workflows.

• 
Familiarity with accounting platforms, ERP systems, CRM systems, and financial data integrity.

• 
Strong problem-solving skills, ownership, and the ability to work independently in a fast-growing environment.

• 
Experience with finance automation or in a startup/scale-up environment is a plus.

About Us

Teton is redefining the role of healthcare workers through cutting-edge AI technology and a great product experience. As populations get older and staff shortages grow, healthcare systems are under pressure. Our mission is to decrease the cost of healthcare while improving the quality of care.

Our product enables care teams to intervene, prevent and operate more efficiently. Our ambient sensors in resident rooms capture activity, sleep, respiration, gait and more. These signals are used both to react fast to risk events, like falls, and for long-term health analysis that care teams can act on.

Teton is scaling fast, operating in the Nordics, UK, DACH and US. We raised a $20M Series A. Expect travel to the US to meet users and team members.

We focus relentlessly on product excellence and user experience, deploying solutions at speed that make a tangible difference for carers. We are an aspiring meritocracy biased towards action, always striving to raise the bar. If you are driven by impact, speed and leveling up, this might be the place for you.

The position requires a physical presence at our office in Copenhagen, Denmark. If you are looking for a 9-17 job, perform best with structure and struggle dealing with unknowns, this is not for you. We believe close collaboration between a hard-working, high-agency team enables the fastest and most efficient iteration cycles, helping us build an impactful product that healthcare professionals truly love to use.

The Job

We're looking for a talented and driven Product Engineer to own customer-facing features from the first conversation with a care team to the feature running in production. Care workers rely on our product during every shift and care managers use it to follow up on their residents, on mobile and on the web. This isn't a ticket-taking role. You'll talk to users, cut scope, build across the whole stack, and check afterwards whether what you shipped actually made a shift easier. Your goal is to shrink the time from a customer request to a deployed solution, without cutting corners on reliability or on the privacy of residents' health data.

In this role, you will focus on:

• 
Feature Development: Own features end-to-end, from design discussions through implementation to production rollout across multiple markets and languages, on the web app, the mobile app and the APIs behind them.

• 
Customer Insight: Talk to care staff and our customer success team every week, visit care facilities, and turn what you hear into clearly scoped product changes. Come with ideas, sketch the solution, and push it forward.

• 
Fast Iteration: Break large designs and features into small shippable pieces. Get MVPs in front of users quickly, measure how they're used, and iterate or kill them.

• 
Backend & APIs: Design and build the APIs, data models and services your features need. You will not just consume APIs, you will help shape, improve and fix the systems behind them.

• 
Quality, Privacy & Safety: Ship with care for health data: sensible access control, auditability and privacy by default. Build test coverage and use staged rollouts so new features never get in the way of the alerts care teams depend on.

Qualifications

• 
Strong TypeScript skills: this is the language for everything we build.

• 
Solid production experience with React on the web and/or React Native.

• 
Comfortable working across the stack: you've built backend APIs and worked with relational databases (e.g. Postgres), not just UI.

• 
Great product taste and a keen eye for UX. You work well with designers and can make sensible design decisions yourself when needed.

• 
Comfortable talking directly with non-technical users and turning messy feedback into concrete decisions.

• 
Previous startup experience and/or shipping a product where you owned the outcome, from idea to adoption.

• 
Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work both independently and in a team.

Nice to Have

• 
Experience with React Native and Expo in production.

• 
AWS or equivalent cloud platform experience.

• 
Familiarity with TanStack, real-time systems or push notifications.

• 
Experience with health data or other regulated, privacy-sensitive domains (e.g. GDPR).

• 
Experience shipping products across multiple markets and languages.

What We Offer

• 
Participation in our warrant program (stock options).

• 
A small team where your decisions directly shape the product.

• 
A Copenhagen-based office with close collaboration, no async-only culture.

• 
Work on software that healthcare workers depend on every day, the impact is tangible and immediate.

Join Our Team

We're looking for individuals who share our vision and value ownership and entrepreneurship over a conventional job.

At Teton, you'll have the chance to make a real impact with your work.

If you're ready for more than just a job, come aboard and be part of our mission to transform healthcare.

Product Specialist - Technical Support & Data Analysis

About ChemoMetec

ChemoMetec is a worldwide leading manufacturer of cell counting and analysis equipment. We specialize in developing and producing high-precision instrumentation, delivering consistent data for thousands of customers across biotech, pharma, and academic segments.

About the Role

We are seeking a highly motivated and analytically skilled Product Specialist - Technical Support & Data Analysis to support customers and colleagues using our cell-counting instruments. In this role, you will combine cell culture biology with data analysis to help users achieve reliable results, investigate unexpected data, and turn insights into product improvements. The ideal candidate holds a PhD in a relevant field, has hands-on cell culture experience, and enjoys working with data in Python.

We are hiring two Product Specialists for our technical support team: one focused on data analysis and one on documentation. You will be part of the Product Management Department and work closely with R&D, QA, Field Application Scientists, and commercial teams. You will provide application and technical support, analyze instrument and experimental data, and contribute to the successful testing and launch of new products.

This position is based at our headquarters. The role includes occasional travel, both domestically and internationally, depending on needs.

Key Responsibilities

• Provide application and technical support for our instruments, helping customers and colleagues with assay setup, sample preparation, and interpretation of results.

• Analyze customer and internal data sets to identify the root causes of unexpected results and recommend solutions.

• Write and maintain Python scripts to automate data analysis, visualization, and reporting.

• Design and analyze experiments and comparison studies for new features and product releases.

• Support product launches with a focus on application readiness, validation data, and training.

• Contribute to technical documentation, including application notes, troubleshooting guides, and data analysis protocols.

• Assist in troubleshooting instrument software, including reading logs to support root cause analysis.

Qualifications

• PhD in Cell Biology, Biotechnology, Biomedical Science, or a related field.

• Hands-on experience with cell culture and common cell-based assays.

• Solid statistical knowledge, including experimental design and method comparison (e.g., precision, linearity, and regression analysis).

• Strong data analysis and data visualization skills.

• Experience with Python scripting for data analysis (e.g., pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib).

• Familiarity with pharmaceutical workflows and regulated lab environments (e.g., GMP) is a strong advantage.

• Structured, curious, and detail-oriented, with a passion for problem-solving.

Preferred Skills

• Experience with software debugging and troubleshooting, such as reading code and log files.

• Experience with cell counting, image cytometry, flow cytometry, or microscopy.

**

Why join ChemoMetec?**

At ChemoMetec, we believe that great people make a great workplace. We value both personal and professional development and offer an environment where you can grow, take responsibility, and make an impact. You will become part of a team of talented and supportive colleagues who enjoy working together in an informal and welcoming atmosphere. We also believe that strong relationships go beyond the workplace, which is why we regularly bring colleagues together through company-wide events to build connections and strengthen relationships across the organization.

**

Practical information**

Both positions are on-site at our HQ in Allerød, Denmark. You will refer to Director, Ph.D. Product Management Bassam Tawfik.

Starting date is as soon as possible, and we conduct interviews on an ongoing basis. Deadline for applying is 20 November 2026.

PEAK Wind is seeking a consultant to support product and project delivery across Data & Intelligence. You will help drive the delivery of our data, analytics, reporting, and digital solutions. This is a hands-on role for someone who can connect clients, renewable energy specialists, and technical teams, and who enjoys taking responsibility from the first conversation to a solution that creates measurable value.

Introducing the Data & Intelligence Team

You will become part of our Data & Intelligence (D&I) team, where we work within PEAK Wind’s operations management service offering and manage full value chain data management for our clients. We support renewable energy assets worldwide through data management, reporting solutions, analytics, digital products, and AI capabilities, helping deliver data-driven solutions that support our clients and renewable energy projects. We support one another, share knowledge, and celebrate both individual and collective achievements.

You will report to the Head of Data & Intelligence and work closely with colleagues across D&I, Asset Management, Engineering, HSEQ, Finance, and Business Development. You will coordinate day-to-day delivery with data engineers, data scientists, developers, and renewable energy specialists, while acting as a clear and trusted point of contact for clients and internal stakeholders.

How You Will Make an Impact

In this role, you will combine product ownership with project delivery, turning business and client needs into well-defined, commercially sound, and successfully delivered D&I solutions. You will take ownership of selected products and projects, create structure around delivery, and ensure that commitments move from proposal and plan to implementation, adoption, and follow-up.

Your work will span both recurring services and new opportunities. This includes day-to-day ownership of selected digital products, coordination of analytics and reporting solutions based on operational and SCADA data, and delivery of selected AI and automation initiatives. You will help ensure that our products and services solve real operational problems rather than becoming isolated technical exercises.

On smaller assignments, you may own the full process from client dialogue and scoping through delivery and handover. On larger assignments, you will work with a multidisciplinary team and keep scope, responsibilities, budget, timeline, quality, and stakeholder expectations aligned. Your key responsibilities will include:

• Own and coordinate selected D&I client projects and internal initiatives from initial need and scoping through delivery, adoption, and follow-up

• Translate operational and commercial challenges into clear requirements, work packages, priorities, acceptance criteria, and delivery plans for technical teams

• Take day-to-day ownership of selected digital products and reporting solutions, including backlog management, stakeholder coordination, implementation planning, user feedback, and continuous improvement

• Coordinate analytics and reporting use cases involving SCADA data, availability, production losses, alarms, asset performance, and operational reporting

• Support proposals and commercial scoping by defining deliverables, assumptions, team setup, effort, pricing input, risks, dependencies, and expected client value

• Act as the link between clients, renewable energy specialists, Product Owners, data engineers, data scientists, and software developers

• Manage delivery governance, including progress tracking, budgets, risks, decisions, actions, dependencies, and clear communication to stakeholders

• Drive selected AI, reporting, and automation initiatives together with technical specialists, ensuring that solutions are useful, governed, and adopted

• Challenge requests constructively, clarify the underlying problem, and recommend a simpler or non-technical solution when that creates better value

• Create clear documentation, client material, handovers, and ways of working so solutions can be operated, supported, and scaled

• Capture lessons learned and contribute to D&I frameworks, templates, playbooks, product roadmaps, and continuous improvement across PEAK Wind

What Will Make You Successful in This Role

At PEAK Wind, we know success comes in many forms. What matters most is your ability to create clarity, build trust, and get valuable work delivered. The following qualities and experiences will help you succeed in this role:

• A degree in engineering, renewable energy, data, business, project management, or a related field, or an equivalent track record from technical consulting or digital delivery

• Experience managing client-facing projects, digital products, analytics solutions, or operational improvement initiatives from scope to implementation

• A strong understanding of project and product delivery, including requirements, prioritisation, planning, budgets, risks, stakeholder management, and handover

• The ability to work across commercial, operational, and technical topics and translate effectively between specialists and decision-makers

• Experience preparing proposals, scopes of work, estimates, presentations, or business cases, with an understanding of how delivery choices affect client value and profitability

• Professional experience in renewable energy, asset management, operational analytics, or another complex technical environment; wind operations, SCADA, availability, or performance reporting experience is a strong advantage

• Familiarity with data and digital products such as Power BI, APIs, cloud platforms, reporting systems, workflow automation, or AI-enabled solutions; hands-on software development is not required

• Clear and effective communication skills in English, both spoken and written, and confidence working directly with clients and senior stakeholders

• A structured and pragmatic approach to problem-solving, with the initiative to create momentum when requirements are incomplete or responsibilities are unclear

• Sound commercial judgement, attention to detail, and the ability to balance quality, timeline, effort, and business value

• A collaborative mindset and the ability to stay calm, constructive, and accountable in an international, cross-functional environment

We care more about your ability to structure ambiguity, build strong relationships, and deliver useful outcomes than about a specific job title or number of years.

Why Join PEAK Wind

• A central role in shaping and delivering data, analytics, reporting, and digital solutions that directly support renewable energy assets and client decision-making

• An international, inclusive, and diverse workplace where differences are valued

• The opportunity to work on leading renewable energy projects alongside experienced industry professionals

• A broad role with direct exposure to clients, commercial decisions, operational challenges, and modern data and AI solutions

• A flat organisational structure where you can take ownership, challenge constructively, and see the result of your work

• A strong focus on your learning, development, and professional growth across product, project, commercial, and renewable energy disciplines

• A culture that values commitment, meaningful contributions, and having fun

Our Commitment to Inclusion and Fair Hiring

We believe that a diverse and inclusive workplace drives innovation, creativity, and stronger results. At PEAK Wind, we are committed to fair and transparent hiring processes, welcoming candidates from all backgrounds, identities, and experiences. Our hiring decisions focus on what each person brings to the role and our team, and we are committed to ensuring transparent salary structures, with pay decisions based on clear, objective, and gender‑neutral criteria. Salary information, including the relevant salary band, will be shared with candidates when they are invited to a first interview.

How to Apply

We look forward to receiving your application. Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis, and we reserve the right to close the recruitment process once the right candidate has been found. Please apply directly through our website. If you have any questions or would like to know more about the position, please contact People & Development at recruitment@peak-wind.com.

PEAK Wind is an independent renewable energy specialist in commercial, financial, and technical operations, delivering advisory, intelligence, and asset management services to investors and developers around the world. From onshore and offshore wind generation to Power-to-X, we work across the entire energy lifecycle to optimise operations and maintenance, enhance asset performance, and provide a holistic view of renewable infrastructure portfolios.

At Aller Aqua Group, we are looking for an ERP Coordinator who enjoys working closely with people across the organization and turning business needs into practical digital solutions.

You will become part of our Group IT team and play an important role in the continued development and optimization of Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central across our international companies.

This is an opportunity to combine your ERP knowledge with collaboration, coordination, and business development in a role where your ideas and contributions will be visible.

The role

As our ERP Coordinator, you will act as a link between users, business functions, external partners, and Group IT.

You will help colleagues get the most from Business Central and contribute to solutions that make every day processes simpler, more consistent, and more effective.

Your responsibilities will include:

• coordinating Business Central projects from initial need to implementation

• understanding business processes and translating user needs into practical solutions

• supporting and advising colleagues on how to use Business Central effectively

• contributing to the design, testing, and implementation of new features and processes

• coordinating activities with external Business Central partners and developers

• ensuring clear documentation and quality assurance

• supporting integrations with other systems

• planning training and providing support to key users

• contributing to the future roadmap and governance of Business Central

What you bring

You may have gained your experience through different roles or career paths. Perhaps you have worked as an ERP consultant, application specialist, system coordinator, finance systems specialist, superuser, or in a business function with responsibility for Business Central.

We would particularly value:

• experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central or an earlier version of NAV

• an understanding of one or more ERP areas, such as finance, purchasing, inventory, production, or sales

• an interest in how systems can support people and business processes

• experience translating business needs into system requirements or improvements

• the ability to communicate clearly with users, managers, and technical specialists

• professional working proficiency in Danish and English

Experience from a manufacturing company is helpful, but it is not essential if you bring relevant ERP and process knowledge from another environment.

Knowledge of international ERP rollouts, reporting, Power BI, SQL, integrations, or data migration would also be welcome. We do not expect you to be an expert in every area from your first day.

Who you are

You create trust and enjoy working with colleagues who have different professional and cultural backgrounds.

You listen, ask questions, and take the time to understand what users need before identifying a solution. You work in a structured way, follow up on your commitments, and are comfortable coordinating several stakeholders.

You are curious and motivated by learning. Most importantly, you enjoy helping people and systems work better together.

What we offer

At Aller Aqua, you will have the opportunity to:

• influence the development of an international ERP platform

• work closely with colleagues across business functions and countries

• develop your knowledge of Business Central and international business processes

• take responsibility while receiving support and professional sparring from your colleagues

• contribute your ideas in an organization where the path from suggestion to action is short

• work under flexible conditions in an informal and collaborative environment

You will become part of Group IT, which currently consists of five colleagues, and report to our Group IT Manager.

Why Aller Aqua?

Aller Aqua is a family-owned company with headquarters in Christiansfeld. We develop and produce fish feed for freshwater and marine aquaculture and serve customers in international markets.

You will join a workplace with colleagues from around the world and become part of a professionally strong team. Here, you can use your experience while continuing to develop your skills and contribute to digital solutions that support our international business.

Our culture is characterized by collaboration, responsibility, innovation, and openness to different perspectives. We believe that our best solutions are created when people share their knowledge and work together across functions and locations.
